sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in Gallatin County, KY?
sections.html:
Three offices in Warsaw matter to a seller. The PVA values the parcel, the Sheriff's Office collects the bill, and the County Clerk records deeds and receives appeals. Gallatin County is small enough that all three sit within a few blocks of one another.

  • PVA: 200 Washington Street (mailing address PO Box 470), Warsaw, KY 41095, phone (859) 567-5621.
  • Sheriff: 106 North Main (PO Box 1025), Warsaw, phone (859) 567-5751. The county website links a tax bill lookup from the sheriff's page.
  • County Clerk: 803 East Main Street, Warsaw, phone (859) 567-5411, open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

The City of Warsaw runs its own online payment page for water, sewer and property tax bills, so a house inside city limits can have a city bill in addition to the county one. Anyone unsure which bills apply to an address should ask the sheriff and the City of Warsaw before closing.

sections.h2: What is Gallatin County like, and why does it matter to a sale?
sections.html:
Gallatin County is one of the smallest in Kentucky, at 105 square miles in total and the second smallest by area. It lies on the Ohio River across from Indiana and belongs to the Cincinnati metropolitan area. The legislature formed it on December 14, 1798 from parts of Franklin and Shelby counties, and later cuts that created Owen, Trimble and Carroll counties left it about a tenth of its original size.

The towns are Warsaw (the seat), Sparta and Glencoe, and the whole county counted as rural in the 2020 census. Interstate 71 crosses it with three exits near Sparta and Glencoe, and US 42 and US 127 also run through. Wikipedia notes that by the 1980s more than half of working residents held jobs outside the county, which is still the pattern: the Census figure for mean travel time to work is 29.5 minutes.

River and race-track landmarks anchor local identity. The Markland Locks and Dam was built between 1956 and 1964, a hydroelectric plant was added in 1967, and the county's own website promotes the Kentucky Speedway and two river marinas. The county-owned Gallatin County Airport, a mile north of Sparta with a 5,000-foot runway, opened in June 2023.

sections.h2: When does Gallatin County want its property tax paid?
sections.html:
Under KRS 134.015, all property tax is due by December 31 of the assessment year, and the sheriff is the payee. A 2 percent discount applies to full payment made by November 1. Face value is owed through December 31. January payments carry 5 percent more, and everything after January 31 carries 10 percent.

If the state delays bill mailing, the Department of Revenue can swap in a shorter schedule: one month at a 2 percent discount, one month at face, one month at plus 5 percent, then 10 percent. Watch the date printed on the bill itself rather than assuming the usual calendar.

Tell the sheriff's office when the house sells, so the next bill reaches the new owner. If a buyer never receives a copy, the sheriff can supply the figures by phone.

sections.h2: How do Gallatin County owners dispute a value?
sections.html:
Kentucky routes every challenge through a PVA conference first. The roll is open for inspection for 13 days beginning on the first Monday in May, so the practical window for a visit to 200 Washington Street is the period after assessment notices arrive and that May inspection stretch.

Once you have met with the PVA or a deputy, the County Clerk's office takes your written appeal. The deadline is the close of business one workday after inspection ends. The local board of assessment appeals then sits for up to five days, starting 25 to 35 days after inspection.

  • Bring facts about the land and buildings, the cost of construction, insurance details and listings of comparable properties.
  • Keep your own audio recording if you want one, since taxpayers have the right to record the hearing.
  • Expect a written explanation for any value the board raises or lowers.

If you skip the board hearing, you lose the path to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

sections.h2: What does the homestead exemption mean for a Gallatin County owner?
sections.html:
Owners aged 65 or older, and those classified as totally disabled, can deduct $49,100 from assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. Applications go to the Gallatin County PVA. For the county's median home value of $178,200, the taxable figure would be $129,100.

The disability version requires payments under a federal or retirement-system program through the whole assessment period and an annual renewal, except for service-connected veterans and people found totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell a Gallatin County house with taxes owed?
sections.html:
The debt stays tied to the parcel. KRS 134.015 makes the tax a personal debt as of the assessment date, and a delinquency lien continues under KRS 134.420 regardless of who holds title.

After April 15, the sheriff passes open bills to the County Clerk as certificates of delinquency. The county attorney sends a notice within 30 days and a second one within 60 days, and the Department of Revenue says a clerk's tax sale falls 90 to 135 days after the transfer. If the certificate is sold at that sale, the third-party buyer can add substantial fees. Ask the sheriff at (859) 567-5751 for a payoff before listing, and plan to clear it from your proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Gallatin County?
faqs.a: Pay the Gallatin County Sheriff, at 106 North Main in Warsaw or PO Box 1025, Warsaw, KY 41095. The PVA's website says its own office cannot accept tax payments.

faqs.q: What is the Gallatin County PVA phone number?
faqs.a: The number is (859) 567-5621, and the office is at 200 Washington Street in Warsaw. Use it for value questions, exemption forms and address changes.

faqs.q: Is the discount deadline different in Gallatin County?
faqs.a: No. It is the statewide date of November 1. Payment in full by then earns 2 percent off, and the full amount is due through December 31.

faqs.q: Does Warsaw charge its own property tax?
faqs.a: Warsaw offers an online page for paying water, sewer and property tax bills. Owners inside the city should ask the city and the sheriff which bills attach to their address.

faqs.q: Can a sold house still carry the seller's tax lien?
faqs.a: Yes. A delinquency lien remains with the property after a sale until the taxes are paid or the lien period under KRS 134.420 ends, so clear the balance at closing.
